id: The Most Dear and The Future
description: Ear is a New York duo of Jonah Paz and Yaelle Avtan, releasing on Surf Gang Records. Their 2025 debut album packs choppy glitch-pop production, punchy synths, and amen breaks into a dense, restless 16 minutes.

Boards of Canada are a Scottish electronic duo who defined a strand of nostalgic, slightly unsettling ambient IDM. Inferno, released in 2026 on Warp Records, is their first album in over a decade and takes a darker, more ominous turn than their earlier work.

Downhill2k01 is a Dallas, Texas producer making jittery IDM and drill and bass with raw MIDI melodies and complex electronic percussion. Pxldll is a focused two-track release showing his tighter, more textural side.
Downhill2k01 is a Dallas producer working in IDM, jungle, and drill and bass. DH Legacy Edition is a 13-track 2021 album contrasting airy synth melodies against dense, jittery percussion.

Photek is the alias of Rupert Parkes, a British producer known for precise, minimalist drum and bass with jazz and techno influences. T'Raenon was released in 1996 on Kirk Degiorgio's Applied Rhythmic Technology label, sitting at the intersection of intelligent drum and bass and techno.

dgoHn is John Cunnane, a UK producer rooted in drumfunk, a drum and bass subgenre centred on intricate breakbeat chopping and jazz-influenced rhythms. Undesignated Proximate, released in 2020 on Love Love Records, collects twelve tracks of inventive, groove-heavy material.

Alex Reece is a British producer who was a key early figure in jazzstep, a melodic strain of drum and bass leaning into jazz samples and smoother bass lines. So Far, released in 1996 on Fourth and Broadway, blends DnB rhythms with lush jazz-funk chord progressions and R&B vocals.

id: A Made Up Sound / The Cult
description: Source Direct were a British drum and bass duo from Hertfordshire, known for dark, atmospheric productions with precise breakbeat construction. This 1995 Metalheadz two-tracker pairs jazz percussion chops on A Made Up Sound with kung fu film samples and midnight jazz chords on The Cult.

Congo Natty is the alias of Michael West, a London producer and toaster with roots in UK sound system culture and Jamaican reggae who has been active in jungle since the early 90s. This Is Jungle compiles classic dub plates and vocal collaborations that define the ragga-jungle sound.

Fila Brazillia are Steve Cobby and David McSherry, an electronic duo from Hull who mix trip hop, funk, and abstract jazz into characterful records. A Touch of Cloth, released in 1999 on their own Tritone label, is one of their more uptempo albums, moving between funky breakbeat grooves, spy-film brass, and gentle ambience.

id: hong kong dub station 香港空轉
description: Released in 2004, the third in the series of albums from Celestial once again invokes a pan-asian dubscape of hypnotic rhythms and deep space textures. Another tectonic phase shift from Celestial merges the sounds of 70’s Jamaican b-sides with top Asian instrumentalists and digital tech-know-how. Rhythms and sounds from dub plates, collide with melodies and textures through zen temple gates.

blurb: Debut album from Julien Loquet recording as Dorine Muraille, released on FatCat Records Splinter series in 2003. Acoustic recordings of double bass, voice, piano and guitar, processed through software into fractured electronic forms.
description: Mani is the debut album by Dorine Muraille, alias of 25-year-old Frenchman Julien Loquet, released in 2003 on FatCat Records’ Splinter series. Drawing on the traditions of Chanson Française and old English folk, it takes acoustic instruments — double bass, voice, piano, guitar — and processes them through software into fractured, glitchy forms. Chloé Delaume provides lyrics and vocals.

blurb: Collaborative EP from Frythm and Lake Hills released on Alpha Pup Records in 2024. Six tracks spanning experimental house, ambient, IDM and 90s Eurodance.
description: Across the Room is a six-track EP from Los Angeles producers Lake Hills and Frythm, released February 2024 on Alpha Pup Records. The duo dance deftly between experimental house, techno, IDM and more — from high-BPM atmospheric euphoria to glitchy introspection to 90s Eurodance club-readiness, with the title track a dark ambient journey featuring vocalist Seyaa.

blurb: Celestial 天上 are a Hong Kong based collective who have produced ten albums of Asian Dubscapes.
description: Celestial 天上 are a Hong Kong based collective who have produced ten albums of Asian Dubscapes.

id: The Ballad of St Nick's Park
blurb: Debut single on XL Recordings blending 300SkullsAndCounting's screamo and chiptune with Jenny Sparks' bassline production. A tribute to a demolished skatepark in Leamington Spa.
description: The Ballad of St Nick's Park is the debut XL Recordings single from 300SkullsAndCounting and London bassline producer Jenny Sparks, released September 2026. The track blends 300SkullsAndCounting's screamo vocals and chiptune with Jenny Sparks' bassline production, paying tribute to a demolished skatepark in Leamington Spa.

blurb: Debut album from New York musician Shane Lavers, released on Jagjaguwar in 2024. Nine tracks blending synthetic and real instruments, released under the Chanel Beads name.
description: Your Day Will Come is the debut album by Chanel Beads, the project of New York-based musician Shane Lavers, released April 2024 on Jagjaguwar. Nine tracks blending synthetic and real instruments into what Lavers describes as 'a memory in which you can't distinguish between what actually happened or what was a false reproduction' — hazy, experimental and deeply felt.

blurb: First album of new material in over fifteen years from Manchester band The Durutti Column, released July 2026. Guitar from Vini Reilly with piano, beats and guest vocals from Caoilfhionn Rose and Lucas Elliot.
description: Renascent is the 28th album by Manchester post-punk outfit The Durutti Column, released July 2026 on London Records — their first new material in over fifteen years. Produced by Keir Stewart, it features Vini Reilly's guitar playing between sonic atmospherics and structure with warm ambient washes, piano, beats and guest vocal turns from Caoilfhionn Rose and Lucas Elliot. The title means rebirth.

blurb: Second album from London-based Ethiopian-British artist Alewya, released June 2026 on LDN Records. 15 tracks of electronic and soul music, with Shy FX as executive producer.
description: Zero is the sophomore album from Alewya, Ethiopian-British singer-songwriter and producer based in London, released June 2026 on LDN Records. Fifteen tracks co-produced with Craigie Dodds and Dean James Barratt, with drum'n'bass icon Shy FX as executive producer — globe-spanning electronic soul moving between dance, R&B and introspective club music.

blurb: Three-track EP on The Bunker New York (BKNY035), released November 2018. Dark hypnotic techno with chanting by Gabriella Vergilov, mastered at EnissLab and pressed at Brooklyn Vinyl Works.
description: Cyberia is the opening track of The Moon Chant EP by Berlin-based producer Marco Shuttle, released November 2018 on The Bunker New York (BKNY035). Three tracks of dark, hypnotic techno featuring chanting by Gabriella Vergilov, mastered at EnissLab and pressed at Brooklyn Vinyl Works.

blurb: Drone-flavoured deep techno EP from Italian producer Alessio Meneghello on Berlin/Prague label Harmony Rec. (HARMONY004), November 2019. Hand painted sleeve by Adam Soukup.
description: Natives is the 2019 EP from Alan Backdrop (Alessio Meneghello), an Italian producer drawing on drone, deep atmosphere and techno. Released on Harmony Rec. (HARMONY004), a label split between Berlin and Prague, with a hand painted sleeve by Adam Soukup and graphic design by Simon Matejka. Four tracks of immersive, deep-rolling techno.

blurb: Four tracks of cloud-named hypnotic techno on Affin LTD (AFFIN046LTD), May 2019. 'Thoughts like clouds. Appearing, expanding, condensing and gushing. Four special moments captured on vinyl.'
description: Noctilucent is a four-track collaborative EP by Dutch producer Reggy Van Oers and German producer Joachim Spieth, released May 2019 on Affin LTD (AFFIN046LTD). Each track is named after a cloud formation — Noctilucent, Cirrus, Undulatus Asperatus, Mammatus — and the record moves through drone ambient and hypnotic deep techno. Artwork by Oliver Keil, mastered at Artefacts Mastering.

blurb: Goa trance release on Cygnetic Records, a Swiss online netlabel presenting free electronic music across goa, psytrance and ambient.
description: Vimana is a goa trance release by Goa Syndrome on Cygnetic Records, a Swiss netlabel that distributed free electronic music across goa, psytrance, ambient and drum'n'bass in the early 2000s.

blurb: WAEREA is the 2024 album from Mokotron, a Tāmaki-based producer from Ngāti Hine. Nine tracks integrating Te Reo Māori, traditional chants and puoro with contemporary breakbeats and basslines, tested on dancefloors across Ōtautahi, Tāmaki and Pōneke before being pressed to 140g vinyl and mastered by Chris Chetland at KOG Studio.

2024 album from Auckland-based producer Christoph El' Truento, drawing on Black Ark-era dub production. Features a large ensemble including drummers, horn players, vocalists and synth programmers, with instrumentation across vibraphone, piano, guitar and lap steel.

LWMP18 is a 2018 21-track album from Auckland producer Christoph El' Truento, released on Banished Music. Blends electronic production with roots reggae and dub across approximately 51 minutes of instrumental and vocal compositions.

Debut studio album from Etran de L'Aïr, a three-brother ensemble and drummer from Agadez, Niger, known as stars of the Aïr region. Recorded in West Coast studios, it brings their Agadez guitar-driven sound into a studio setting for the first time after years on the local wedding circuit and international touring. Released on Sahel Sounds in September 2024.

Second album from Les Filles de Illighadad, fronted by Fatou Seidi Ghali, one of the only female Tuareg guitarists in Niger. Blends traditional tende drum and calabash percussion with guitar-driven arrangements and polyphonic vocals, recorded in Illighadad village in central Niger. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2017.
1997 self-titled album from Japanese techno and breakbeat outfit Terrace Brothers + Asa.
あと何日 (How Many More Days) is a 1995 track by Tokyo pop duo Hi-Posi, from their album Body Meets Sing on Kitty Records. Shibuya-kei influenced pop with ambient undertones.

Opening track of Charanjit Singh's 1982 album Synthesizing: Ten Ragas to a Disco Beat, recorded at HMV Studios in Bombay using Roland Jupiter-8, TB-303 and TR-808. The record is considered an accidental precursor to acid house, predating the Chicago scene by several years. Reissued in 2010 on Bombay Connection.

Film soundtrack by Shinichi Tanabe for the 1979 Kon Ichikawa mystery film Byouinzaka no Kubikukuri no Ie (The House of Hanging on Hospital Hill), based on Seishi Yokomizo's novel and distributed by Toho. Released on Chat Noir / Toho Records.

1995 goa trance track by Danish producer Kristian Thinning Andersen as Elysium, released on Avatar Records. A classic of the old-school goa trance scene, later compiled on the album Dance For The Celestial Beings.
1998 album by Kaori Kano under the name Cocu (コキュウ), featuring Yen Chang, released on Polyster Records. Recorded at Yen Studio in Tokyo, blending ambient textures, natural sounds and pop.

Baby Night is one of two side-length tracks on Just a Poke, the 1970 debut album by Sweet Smoke, a group of New York musicians who relocated to Germany. Engineered by Conny Plank and released on EMI Harvest, it runs over 16 minutes blending psychedelic rock and free jazz.

Shinichi Atobe's mysterious 2001 debut, originally released as an untitled demo on Chain Reaction before being reissued as Ship Scope. Hazy, submerged dub techno that quietly influenced a generation of ambient and deep house producers.
1996 collaboration between trip hop pioneer DJ Krush and avant-garde trumpeter Toshinori Kondo, fusing hip hop beats with free jazz improvisation years ahead of the jazz-hop movement it anticipated.
1995 debut album from Ninja Tune's DJ Food collective, a dense, sample-heavy collage of trip hop breaks and turntablism built by Coldcut's Strictly Kev and PC.
Warm, broken-beat flavored future jazz from German project Moodorama, blending live instrumentation with deep downtempo electronics from the early-2000s scene.
Lush, healing new age ambience from Japanese artist Dream Dolphin, layering crystalline synth textures over gentle trance pulses.
Early-70s dub from Lee 'Scratch' Perry and The Upsetters, built at the Black Ark studio with heavy echo, reverb and reversed tape effects that helped define the dub genre.
1996 album from Warp Records duo B12, a key document of mid-90s British IDM and electro, all crisp machine rhythms and glassy synth melodies.

MINNA, a London-based artist, hails from the Scottish Borders. Immersed in a house of pianists and songwriters, she developed a profound connection to folk music from an early age. She has spent the last year recording in London and LA, gigging at every opportunity, most notably supporting Russel Crowe, Newton Faulkner and Izo Fitzroy at Union Chapel.

Second album from Etran de L'Aïr, the long-running wedding band from Agadez, Niger, made up of brothers and cousins. Hypnotic solos and surf-tinged melodies celebrating their desert hometown, and the record that launched them onto the international touring circuit. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2022.

Underground hip hop from Niamey's Mamaki Boys, formed in 2002, built from sampled village percussion and chopped-up traditional instruments with a ragga-inspired flow. A product of the DIY studio boom of early-2000s West Africa. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2021.

Live recording of Les Filles de Illighadad at Pioneer Works in Brooklyn, the all-female-led Tuareg group from a remote village in central Niger. Guitar and tende percussion stretched into long hypnotic jams. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2021.

Debut album from Wau Wau Collectif, recorded in the Senegalese village of Toubab Dialaw. Draws on Sufi praise songs, spiritual jazz and dub, with percussion loops, call and response chants, children's voices and electronic beats. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2021.

One of the first full-length recordings of Hauka ritual music from Niger, the spirit possession movement documented in Jean Rouch's 1955 film Les maîtres fous. Call and response chants, monochord lute and relentless percussion in one nonstop session. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2020.

Dreamy instrumental acoustic guitar from Tidiane Thiam of Podor in northern Senegal. His intricate fingerpicking is inspired by the four-string hoddu lute, a distinctly different style of Sahelian guitar from the familiar desert blues. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2020.

Rare 1990s studio recording from El Wali, the Sahrawi political folk group of the Polisario movement. Traditional modes mixed with synthesizer, programmed drums and electric guitar, with anthems and call and response duets. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2019.

Reissue of a 1995 cassette by Abdallah Ag Oumbadougou, one of the founders of Tuareg guitar music and a figure of the 1990s Tuareg rebellion. Recorded in Benin, it is one of the first studio recordings of the genre, with a full 90s groove. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2019.

Second album from Bamako producer Luka Guindo as Luka Productions, focused on Manding cultural heritage. Griots and ngoni players join him in the studio over sweeping synth pads and sequenced drums. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2019.

Instrumental electronic keyboard from Ahmedou Ahmed Lowla, one of Mauritania's leading players of WZN, the synth music that soundtracks weddings in Nouakchott. His father was a renowned tidinit lute player. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2019.

Stripped-down solo acoustic guitar from Ahmed Ag Kaedy of Amanar de Kidal, recorded in exile from his northern Malian hometown. Melancholic ballads and pleas for peace for a community divided by civil war. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2019.

Nigerien composer Hama reimagines nomadic herding ballads, caravan songs and wedding chants as electronic music somewhere between early-90s techno and synthwave, like a soundtrack to a Tuareg video game. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2019.

Soundtrack to Zerzura, billed as the first Saharan acid Western, composed by its lead actor Ahmoudou Madassane. Free-form guitar improvisations recorded while watching the film, turning Tuareg guitar into ambient soundscapes. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2018.

Takamba from Timbuktu's Tallawit Timbouctou, built around the four-string tehardent lute through handmade mics and blown-out amplifiers, over calabash percussion in mind-bending time signatures. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2018.

1980s recordings of an all-girl elementary school group from the Tudu neighbourhood of Agadez, accompanied by their instructor, Tuareg guitarist Kader 'Barmo' Balla. Recalls Guinean folk and early Ali Farka Touré. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2018.

Debut album from Etran de L'Aïr, 'the Stars of the Aïr', one of the longest-playing wedding bands in Agadez, Niger. Raw, surf-tinged electric guitar recorded in their home. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2018.

Takamba from Agali Ag Amoumine's group Tallawit Timbouctou, sent directly from Timbuktu over the internet. Teheredent lute and calabash rhythms, the traditional festival and wedding music of northern Mali. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2018.

Ambient field recordings from across the western Sahel: desert oases, late-night radio, village calls to prayer and riverboats on the Niger. A companion to the label's musical releases. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2018.

Album from Group Afous d'Afous of Tamanrasset, Algeria, stars of Tuareg guitar at home but almost unknown outside the Sahara. Electric guitar from the contemporary pop side of the desert blues sound. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2017.

id: Gao Rap - Hip Hop from Northern Mali
blurb: Compilation of the hyper-local electronic hip hop of Gao in northeastern Mali, mixing autotune, melodic synths and PC beats with takamba drones, Hausa synth pop and ragga. Music that lives on the local MP3 trade. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2017.

Contemporary field recordings of guitar music across Niger, from meditative ballads and fuzzy Hendrix covers to wedding bands and political folk guitarists, collected over years of travel. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2017.

New age music from West Africa by Bamako rapper and producer Luka Guindo. Cut-up kora and balafon over software percussion, flute and synthesizer, with field recordings and spoken affirmations. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2017.

artist: Jeich Ould Badu and Ahmedou Ahmed Lewla
blurb: Instrumental synth and lute from two stars of Mauritanian WZN: griot Jeich Ould Badu on a hacked traditional lute with built-in phasers, and synth player Ahmedou Ahmed Lewla. Playful drum machines and organ freakouts. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2017.

artist: Amadou Binta Konté and Tidiane Thiam
blurb: Improvised session of acoustic guitar and hoddu lute from Fouta Toro, drawing on ancient praise songs and epic ballads, recorded in a fishing village in northern Senegal. First release on the Sahel Sounds and Mississippi Records imprint Songs from Home, 2017.

Compilation of kologo music from Bolgatanga in northern Ghana, the two-string lute tradition championed by King Ayisoba. Sung in Frafra and pidgin English, from solo kologo to full bands. Released with Makkum Records and Red Wig Records in 2016.

First official release of one of the biggest songs in contemporary Saharan music, Kader Tarhanine's love song with electric guitar and drum machine that made Afous d'Afous stars of Tuareg guitar in Algeria. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2016.

Archival recordings from Azna de L'Ader, possibly the first rock band in Niger and certainly the most psychedelic. Led by Hendrix-inspired guitarist Mona, with shrieking fuzz solos over local rhythms, often called West Africa's answer to Zamrock. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2016.

Studio album from Kidal's Amanar, delayed for years by conflict in northern Mali. Rolling rhythms, wistful melodies and call and response vocals, songs about change, nostalgia and hope from a band in exile. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2016.

Future beats from Bamako rapper and producer Luka, with rapid-fire raps over balafon samples and synths, mixing Malian tradition with décalé and club rhythms. Features guest MCs from across the Bamako scene. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2016.

Raucous, electrified wedding music from Mauritania, with microtonal scales, phaser pedals and unpredictable polyrhythms. Desert music as it is actually performed, loud and unfiltered. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2015.

Self-produced album from Niger Tuareg rock outfit TisDass, led by Kildjate Moussa Albadé, former bassist for Bombino. Looping electric guitar and two-chord rhythms, covers and originals in the assouf tradition. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2015.

Early recordings from Nigerien electronic pioneer Mamman Sani: unreleased tracks from his first album, a short-lived trio and a cover of an American folk ballad. Dreamy organs and droning melodies reinterpreting Saharan folk. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2015.

Mixtape from DJ Sandji, an innovator of Bamako's Balani Show street party scene. Bassy balafon cut-ups and décalé rhythms with live drums added on the fly from a sampler. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2015.

Lo-fi Tuareg guitar from Timbuktu musician Abba Gargando, from electrified weddings to quiet fireside sessions in refugee camps. Recorded on cellphones, the medium where he is best known. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2015.

id: Uchronia – Field Recordings From Alternate Realities
blurb: Fictional ethnography of an alternate Bamako where the 14th-century Malian king Abubakari II 'discovered' America. Future Manding, Bamako nu-wave and hip hop, made with photographer Maciek Pozoga, Christopher Kirkley and Bamako artists. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2015.

First official release from Supreme Talent Show, kings of Bamako's sound system street party scene. Cut-up balafon, djembe and talking drum samples in a Malian mix of kuduro, décalé, dancehall and trap. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2015.

Debut recording from Fadimoutou Wallet Inamoud, a 2008 local production of isswat, the Tuareg vocal music of nostalgia and revolution from the Azawad region. Sparse rhythms and hand claps under a hypnotic group vocal drone. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2015.
Gritty, high-energy Tuareg guitar from Kidal's hometown band Amanar, recorded at a local studio in 2008 during an uprising. The title means 'Peace'. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2015.

Debut release from Nigerien synthesizer composer Hama, known at home through unlabelled memory-card releases. Draws on North African synth, Tuareg tishumaren, 90s Nigerien hip hop and Detroit techno. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2015.

Cosmic synth from Mamman Sani: polyphonic analog synthesizers and drum machines interpreting ancient Saharan folk ballads, somewhere between ambient library music and minimal wave. Recorded in Niger and France in the late 1980s. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2014.

id: Balani Show Super Hits: Electronic Street Parties from Mali
blurb: Compilation of tracks from Bamako's Balani Show street parties, which began in the late 90s when DJs with big sound systems replaced live balafon players. A decade of the scene's hits. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2014.

Electrified takamba sessions from Gao's Super Onze, recorded in the early 90s. Shredding traditional lute over staccato calabash percussion, with tape hiss and pickup distortion. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2013.
Full-length from Gao rapper Pheno S., first heard on Music from Saharan Cellphones. Autotuned raps, pitch-bending soft synths and glitchy homemade beats. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2013.

Recorded in Kidal, Mali, in 2008 at a Tuareg-run studio later destroyed by Islamist occupiers. Idassane Wallet Mohamed sings love songs and songs of nomadic life over tende rhythms. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2013.

id: Harafin So - Bollywood Inspired Film Music from Hausa Nigeria
blurb: Soundtrack music from Kannywood, the Bollywood-inspired film industry of Kano in northern Nigeria. Autotuned vocals, frenetic drum machines and pitch-bending synths, collected on a 2012 trip to Kano. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2013.
Minimal organ instrumentals from Mamman Sani, a pioneer of West African electronic music whose music has filled Nigerien radio and TV intermissions for decades. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2013.

Recordings from Mauritania's national orchestra, formed in 1968 and trained in Guinea under Bembeya Jazz. Added electric guitars and brass to the strict modal system of Mauritanian classical music. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2013.

Second volume of pop music collected from cellphones in northern Mali in 2010, from Niger guitar ballads and Bamako club music to Moroccan raï, with a focus on autotuned DIY productions. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2013.
Compilation of guitar music from Mauritania, Senegal and Mali, selected from three years of field recordings, from riverside houses on the Niger to desert campfires. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2012.

Garage rock from Alkibar Junior (Alkibar Gignor), formed as apprentices to Afel Bocoum's band and now the town band of Niafunké. Got their break opening Ali Farka Touré's memorial festival. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2012.
Debut from Tallawit Timbouctou, led by Agali Ag Amoumine, playing takamba, the hypnotic lute and calabash music of northern Mali. Released by Sahel Sounds with Little Axe Records in 2012.

First full-length from Lewlewal de Podor, a Pulaar guitar band from northern Senegal drawing on the folk styles of Fouta Toro, from mellow acoustic jams to electrified concerts. Released by Sahel Sounds with Little Axe Records in 2011.

id: L'Orchestre National de Mauritanie - La Mone / Kamlat
blurb: Two-track single from Mauritania's national orchestra, mixing electric guitar and brass with Mauritanian modal music. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2011.

The first Sahel Sounds compilation: guitar bands from Fouta Toro, Timbuktu and the Adrar des Ifoghas in Senegal and Mali, almost unknown outside their regions but with devoted local followings. Released in 2010.

Final album in Wau Wau Collectif's trilogy, the cross-cultural project begun in Toubab Dialaw in 2018 by Senegalese musician Arouna Kane and Swedish producer Karl-Jonas Winqvist. Named for the Wolof word for hospitality, it finds the collective recording together for the first time. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2026.

Self-produced studio album from Bamako-based Tuareg band Amanar de Kidal, years in the making and recorded in small studios in the Malian capital. Carries on the assouf guitar tradition of Tinariwen with tighter, more upbeat grooves. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2026.

Live recording of a little-known contemporary Bamako bar band led by Mohamed Doumbia, paying tribute to the Malian orchestras of the late 60s and 70s that produced Salif Keita and Kante Manfila. Soulful vocals, psychedelic solos and Afro-Latin rhythms. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2026.
Two remixes of tracks from Namian Sidibé's 2023 self-titled album, including UK duo BOM Nation's melodic electronic take on the acapella closer 'Môgôya'. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2026.

Official release of two of the most popular songs by Agadez singer-songwriter Mohamed Alassane Karzo, 'Mafelawen' and 'C'est La Vie', recorded in Niger in 2012. Karzo's full chord progressions stand out in the Tuareg guitar repertoire. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2025.

Solo instrumental guitar album from Tidiane Thiam of Podor in northern Senegal, built around the title's message that it is time for Africa to take its destiny into its own hands. Fingerpicked Pulaar guitar from the Fouta Toro region. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2024.

Full-length debut from Malian guitar hero Bounaly (Ali Traore), first heard on Music from Saharan WhatsApp. Recorded live on location, it mixes regional favourites, traditional standards and originals with looping rhythms and shredding electric guitar. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2023.

First internationally distributed studio recording from Andal Sukabe, a Wodaabe family band of siblings from Niamey, Niger, following their appearance on Music from Saharan WhatsApp. Guitar and polyphonic vocals rooted in nomadic Wodaabe tradition. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2023.

Intimate, stripped-down session from young Malian singer Namian Sidibé, accompanied by her cousin Jules Diabaté on acoustic guitar and recorded at her home. Traditional Wassoulou praise songs and poetry brought into the social media age. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2023.

First solo release from Baba 'Babsy' Konate, a key producer in the autotuned Songhoi style known as Gao Rap. Collects a decade of tracks merging sweet vocals, crunchy drum loops and plucked digital harpsichord. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2023.

Debut EP from young Agadez guitarist Moussa Tchingou, who learned to play at 12 on a homemade guitar built from a water jug and motorcycle clutch cable, and is now one of the most in-demand wedding guitarists in town. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2023.

Second album from Wau Wau Collectif, the long-distance collaboration between Senegalese musicians led by Arouna Kane and Sweden's Karl-Jonas Winqvist. Children's songs collide with fuzzy guitar solos, hip-hop beats and shimmering synths. Released on Sahel Sounds in 2022.
Album from Afro-Peruvian singer Susana Baca, recorded live in a New York studio with guests including Marc Ribot and Bill Frisell. Released on Luaka Bop in 2002, reissued 2023.
Debut album from Milwaukee soul and funk band Kings Go Forth, led by Andy Noble of Lotus Land Records, part of the late-2000s soul revival. Released on Luaka Bop in 2010.
Reissue of Jim White's 1997 debut, The Mysterious Tale of How I Shouted Wrong-Eyed Jesus!, from the storytelling, taxi-driving former Pentecostal from Pensacola, Florida. Southern gothic alt-country.

id: Brazil 5: The Return of Tom Zé: The Hips of Tradition
blurb: 1992 album from Tom Zé, the avant-garde tropicália veteran from Bahia, originally titled Ancas. His second Luaka Bop release after David Byrne rediscovered him, reissued for its 30th anniversary.

id: Brazil Classics 4: The Best of Tom Zé - Massive Hits
blurb: 1990 compilation of Tom Zé's 70s recordings, assembled by David Byrne after he found one of Zé's records in a Rio shop. It relaunched Zé's career outside Brazil. Released on Luaka Bop.

id: Dance Raja Dance: The South Indian Film Music of: Asia Classics 1
blurb: Compilation of 80s Telugu and Kannada film songs produced by South Indian music director Vijaya Anand, one of the first to use electronic instruments in Indian film scores. Released on Luaka Bop in 1992.

id: Peppermint Tea House: The Best Of Shoukichi Kina - Asia Classics 2
blurb: Best-of from Okinawan musician Shoukichi Kina and his band Champloose, mixing Okinawan folk with rock, featuring Ry Cooder. Released on Luaka Bop in 1994.

Fourth of Alhaji Waziri Oshomah's Volume Series, recorded 1978-1984 at the peak of his career: Muslim highlife from Afemailand in Edo State, Nigeria, mixing Etsako folk with highlife and Islamic sermonising.

Fifth of Alhaji Waziri Oshomah's Volume Series, recorded 1978-1984 at the peak of his career: Muslim highlife from Afemailand in Edo State, Nigeria, mixing Etsako folk with highlife and Islamic sermonising.

Third of Alhaji Waziri Oshomah's Volume Series, recorded 1978-1984 at the peak of his career: Muslim highlife from Afemailand in Edo State, Nigeria, mixing Etsako folk with highlife and Islamic sermonising.

Second of Alhaji Waziri Oshomah's Volume Series, recorded 1978-1984 at the peak of his career: Muslim highlife from Afemailand in Edo State, Nigeria, mixing Etsako folk with highlife and Islamic sermonising. Includes 17-minute praise songs.

First of Alhaji Waziri Oshomah's Volume Series, recorded 1978-1984 at the peak of his career: Muslim highlife from Afemailand in Edo State, Nigeria, mixing Etsako folk with highlife and Islamic sermonising.
EP from Pastor Champion, the Oakland outsider gospel preacher and electric guitarist, including 'Song For My Brother'. Released on Luaka Bop in 2022.
1975 album from the Staples Jr. Singers, a family group of teenagers from Aberdeen, Mississippi, who played raw, funky soul gospel. Originally self-released, reissued on Luaka Bop in 2022.

id: I Just Want To Be A Good Man
blurb: Live recordings of Pastor Champion (1946-2021), an outsider gospel singer raised in the Jim Crow South who travelled with his electric guitar to congregations from San Jose to Shreveport. Released on Luaka Bop in 2022.
The first Luaka Bop release, compiled by David Byrne in 1989: MPB and tropicália from Caetano Veloso, Gilberto Gil, Jorge Ben, Milton Nascimento and more. It reached the Billboard 200.
Album from Danish duo Bremer/McCoy, bassist Jonathan Bremer and keyboardist Morten McCoy, inspired by the end of the day. Slow, dubby instrumental jazz. Released on Luaka Bop in 2021.

artist: Floating Points, Pharoah Sanders & The London Symphony Orchestra
blurb: A single continuous nine-movement piece composed by Floating Points for saxophonist Pharoah Sanders and the London Symphony Orchestra, Sanders' last major recording. Released on Luaka Bop in 2021.

id: World Psychedelic Classics 5: Who is William Onyeabor?
blurb: Compilation introducing William Onyeabor, the reclusive Nigerian synth-funk pioneer who self-released his records from Enugu in the late 70s and early 80s. Released on Luaka Bop in 2013.

id: World Psychedelic Classics 4: Nobody Can Live Forever – The Existential Soul of Tim Maia
blurb: Compilation of Tim Maia's mid-70s Racional period, when the Brazilian soul giant joined a UFO cult and self-released two albums of deep funk. Released on Luaka Bop in 2012.
Album from Danish duo Bremer/McCoy, bass and keys with Wurlitzer, piano and dubbed-out textures, including the single 'Højder'. Released on Luaka Bop in 2020.

id: World Spirituality Classics 2: The Time For Peace Is Now
blurb: Compilation of 1970s American soul gospel from small-label and private-press groups, singing about peace and social change rather than straight scripture. Released on Luaka Bop in 2019.

id: Universal Philosophy: Preacherman Plays T.J. Hustlers Greatest Hits
blurb: Outsider funk and soul from Oakland's T.J. Hustler (Mr. Jones) under his Preacherman alias, homemade drum machine grooves and sermons. Released on Luaka Bop in 2018.
Solo album from Rio producer and bassist Alexandre Kassin, with songs about his divorce including the dark bossa nova 'A Paisagem Morta'. Released on Luaka Bop in 2018.

id: The Good is a Big God
blurb: Album from Rio multi-instrumentalist Domenico Lancellotti, of the +2 trio with Kassin and Moreno Veloso. Gentle, off-kilter Brazilian pop. Released on Luaka Bop in 2018.
Private-press devotional soul from John 'Panduranga' Henderson, a former keyboardist in Ray Charles' band who became a Hare Krishna devotee. Reissued on Luaka Bop in 2018.

id: The Atomic Bomb Band Plays the Music of William Onyeabor
blurb: Live studio recording of the Atomic Bomb Band, assembled to perform William Onyeabor's music since he never played it live, with members including Sinkane, Money Mark and Pat Mahoney. Released on Luaka Bop in 2017.
Two long tracks from Floating Points' live band, the title track a 17-minute jam that built out of his album Elaenia. Released in 2016.
Floating Points and his band recorded live in the Mojave Desert near Joshua Tree, released with a film of the sessions. Released in 2017.

id: World Spirituality Classics 1: The Ecstatic Music of Alice Coltrane Turiyasangitananda
blurb: Compilation of devotional music Alice Coltrane recorded at her ashram in the 80s and 90s as Turiyasangitananda: synths, organ and ecstatic Sanskrit chanting. Released on Luaka Bop in 2017.
Janka Nabay, the Sierra Leonean modernizer of bubu music, a traditional processional music played on bamboo pipes, recorded in Brooklyn. Released on Luaka Bop in 2017.
Debut album from Floating Points (Sam Shepherd), bridging his dance music with classical roots through modular synths, a Fender Rhodes and live band. Released on Pluto in 2015.

id: Atomic Bomb by Hot Chip remixed by John Talabot
blurb: Remix EP from William Onyeabor's catalog, featuring John Talabot reworking Hot Chip's cover of 'Atomic Bomb'. Released on Luaka Bop in 2016.
1978 album from William Onyeabor, the reclusive Nigerian synth-funk pioneer who self-released his records from Enugu in the late 70s and early 80s. Reissued on Luaka Bop.
1985 album from William Onyeabor, the reclusive Nigerian synth-funk pioneer who self-released his records from Enugu in the late 70s and early 80s. Reissued on Luaka Bop.

Re-recorded, more electronic version of Crashes In Love by William Onyeabor, the reclusive Nigerian synth-funk pioneer who self-released his records from Enugu in the late 70s and early 80s.
The original, mostly acoustic version of Crashes In Love (1977) by William Onyeabor, the reclusive Nigerian synth-funk pioneer who self-released his records from Enugu in the late 70s and early 80s.
1980 album from William Onyeabor, the reclusive Nigerian synth-funk pioneer who self-released his records from Enugu in the late 70s and early 80s. Side A is 'Let's Fall In Love', side B 'Good Name'.

1979 album from William Onyeabor, the reclusive Nigerian synth-funk pioneer who self-released his records from Enugu in the late 70s and early 80s. Reissued on Luaka Bop.

id: My Name Is Doug Hream Blunt
blurb: Compilation of Doug Hream Blunt, who took up guitar at 35 in an adult class in a San Francisco garage in the late 80s and self-released dreamy lo-fi soul. Released on Luaka Bop in 2016.
Second solo album from Moreno Veloso, son of Caetano Veloso and member of the +2 trio. Released on Luaka Bop in 2014.
Remix album of William Onyeabor songs by Hot Chip, Caribou, Daphni, Javelin and others. Released on Luaka Bop in 2014.
Album from Providence duo Javelin, cousins Tom Van Buskirk and George Langford, making sample-heavy, melodic party pop. Released on Luaka Bop in 2013.
Second album from New Jersey guitarist Delicate Steve (Steve Marion), joyful slide-guitar instrumentals written and played entirely by himself. Released on Luaka Bop in 2012.
Debut album from Bright Moments, the project of multi-instrumentalist Kelly Pratt, recorded track by track in his New York apartment over the winter of 2010. Released on Luaka Bop in 2011.
Debut album from New Jersey guitarist Delicate Steve, bright instrumental guitar pop. Released on Luaka Bop in 2011.
Tom Zé's deconstruction and celebration of bossa nova, the 1958 movement that turned Brazil into an exporter of art. Released on Luaka Bop in 2010.
Debut album from Providence duo Javelin, genre-hopping sample pop born from warehouse parties. Released on Luaka Bop in 2010.
Six-song EP from Susana Baca, partly a tribute to Peruvian composer Chabuca Granda, who wrote 'Don't forget me, sing me' to Baca from her deathbed. Released on Luaka Bop in 2009.

id: A Society In Which No Tear Is Shed Is Inconceivably Mediocre
blurb: Bedroom recordings by Vinicius Gageiro Marques (Yonlu), a teenage songwriter from Porto Alegre who died in 2006 aged 16. Lo-fi bossa nova and indie folk. Released on Luaka Bop in 2009.
Third album of the +2 trilogy, credited to Kassin +2 with Moreno Veloso and Domenico Lancellotti, drawing on Rio's MPB, tropicália and bossa nova. Released on Luaka Bop in 2007.

id: Brazil Classics 7: What’s Happening In Pernambuco: New Sounds of the Brazilian Northeast
blurb: Compilation of the manguebeat-era scene from Recife, Pernambuco, mixing northeastern rhythms with electronics and rock. Released on Luaka Bop in 2008.

id: A Funny Little Cross To Bear
blurb: Mini-album of live roadside rarities from Jim White recorded at record stores, radio sessions and concert halls, including 'Jim 3:16'. Released on Luaka Bop in 2008.
Os Mutantes' 2006 reunion concert at London's Barbican, their first show together in over 30 years. Released on Luaka Bop in 2007.
Susana Baca traces Afro-Peruvian music's connections across the African diaspora, from Chorrillos to the Caribbean and beyond. Released on Luaka Bop in 2011.
Jim White's fourth album, named for the feeling of joy after years of feeling lost, produced with Joe Pernice and Ollabelle. Released on Luaka Bop in 2007.
Tom Zé's operetta on the oppression of women, built around the pagode samba style. Released on Luaka Bop in 2005.
Second album of the +2 trilogy, credited to Domenico +2 with Kassin and Moreno Veloso. Playful Rio pop with electronics. Released on Luaka Bop in 2003.
Zap Mama's 2004 album, with Marie Daulne collaborating with Erykah Badu, Common, Talib Kweli and Questlove. Released on Luaka Bop.

id: World Psychedelic Classics, Vol. 3: Love’s A Real Thing: The Funky Fuzzy Sounds of West Africa
blurb: Compilation of early-70s West African psychedelic funk from Nigeria, Ghana, Benin and beyond, fuzz guitars and heavy grooves. Released on Luaka Bop in 2005.

id: Cuisine Non-Stop: Introduction to The French Nouvelle Generation
blurb: Compilation of France's nouvelle chanson scene, including Lo'Jo, Les Têtes Raides and Mathieu Boogaerts, mixing chanson with world music. Released on Luaka Bop in 2002.

artist: Janka Nabay and The Bubu Gang
blurb: Debut album from Janka Nabay and the Bubu Gang, Brooklyn musicians backing the Sierra Leonean singer's electrified bubu music. Released on Luaka Bop in 2012.
First album of the +2 trilogy, credited to Moreno Veloso +2 with Kassin and Domenico Lancellotti. Moreno is the son of Caetano Veloso. Released on Luaka Bop in 2001.

id: Push It To The Max EP
blurb: EP from Zap Mama, Marie Daulne's Belgian-Congolese vocal group. Released on Luaka Bop in 2001.
Jim White's second album, Southern gothic storytelling with producers including Morcheeba and Q-Burns Abstract Message. Released on Luaka Bop in 2001.
Second album from Mexico City's Los De Abajo, mixing ska, cumbia, son jarocho and punk. Released on Luaka Bop in 2002.
Debut album from New York duo Si*Sé, mixing hip-hop beats, Latin rhythms and downtempo electronica with Carol C's vocals. Released on Luaka Bop in 2001.
Susana Baca's 2000 album, produced by Craig Street, blending Afro-Peruvian rhythms with contributions from Marc Ribot and John Medeski. Released on Luaka Bop.
Zap Mama's 1999 album, Marie Daulne's group moving further into soul and hip hop. Released on Luaka Bop.
Zap Mama's 1994 second album, the Belgian-Congolese female vocal group's polyphonic a cappella drawing on African and European traditions. Released on Luaka Bop.
Remixes of Tom Zé's Fabrication Defect by artists including Tortoise's John McEntire, Sean Lennon and Amon Tobin, plus the outtake 'Canudos'. Released on Luaka Bop in 1999.
Second Luaka Bop album from Caracas disco-funk band Los Amigos Invisibles, mixing acid jazz, bossa nova and house. Released in 2000.

id: In Spite of Wishing and Wanting
blurb: David Byrne's score for the Ultima Vez dance company production by Wim Vandekeybus, based on stories by Julio Cortázar. Released on Luaka Bop in 1999.

id: Beleza Tropical 2: Novo! Mais! Melhor! - Brazil Classics 6
blurb: Sequel to Beleza Tropical, compiled by David Byrne, covering 90s Brazilian pop from Carlinhos Brown, Chico Science, Marisa Monte and others. Released on Luaka Bop in 1998.

id: Com Defeito de Fabricação: Fabrication Defect
blurb: Tom Zé's 1998 album, a concept record about 'defective' Third World workers using sampling and found sounds. Released on Luaka Bop.
Solo album from Mimi Goese, singer of 80s minimalist group Hugo Largo, who also sang on Moby's Everything is Wrong. Released on Luaka Bop in 1998.

id: The New Sound of the Venezuelan Gozadera
blurb: US debut from Caracas band Los Amigos Invisibles, a party record of funk, house, acid jazz and bossa nova. Released on Luaka Bop in 1998.
Self-titled 1997 album from Afro-Peruvian singer Susana Baca, her international debut. Released on Luaka Bop.
Zap Mama's 1997 album, Marie Daulne's move from a cappella to a collective mixing hip hop, jungle, reggae and pygmy chants. Released on Luaka Bop.
International debut from Angolan singer Waldemar Bastos, recorded in New York with Angolan and Portuguese musicians and produced by Arto Lindsay. Released on Luaka Bop in 1997.
Second album from Pomona, California trio Geggy Tah (Tommy Jordan, Greg Kurstin, Daren Hahn), including the hit 'Whoever You Are'. Released on Luaka Bop in 1996.
Second album from New York Latin ska band King Changó, led by Venezuelan singer Andrew Blanco, a tribute to Mexican wrestler El Santo. Released on Luaka Bop in 2000.

id: Afro-Peruvian Classics: The Soul of Black Peru
blurb: Compilation of music from Peru's Black coastal communities, including Susana Baca's 'Maria Landó', which introduced her to the world. Released on Luaka Bop in 1995.

id: Blue In The Face - Music From The Miramax Motion Picture
blurb: Soundtrack to Wayne Wang and Paul Auster's 1995 film Blue in the Face, with music from David Byrne, Lou Reed and others. Released on Luaka Bop.
Debut from New York Latin ska band King Changó, mixing dancehall, dub, ska and Latin rhythms. Released on Luaka Bop in 1996.
Final album from A.R. Kane, the London duo who coined 'dream pop' and pioneered a mix of noise, dub and soul. Released on Luaka Bop in 1994.
Zap Mama's debut, the Belgian-Congolese female a cappella group led by Marie Daulne singing polyphony drawn from African and European traditions. Released on Luaka Bop in 1993.
Compilation of early-90s Cuban dance music, a new generation's take on son and salsa. Released on Luaka Bop in 1992.
US compilation of A.R. Kane, Alex Ayuli and Rudy Tambala's pioneering dream pop and noise. Released on Luaka Bop in 1992.
Luaka Bop's first label sampler, collecting the most popular tracks from its first two years. Released in 1991.

id: Cuba Classics 1: The Best of Silvio Rodríguez
blurb: Best-of from Silvio Rodríguez, the Cuban singer-songwriter at the heart of the nueva trova movement. Released on Luaka Bop in 1991.

id: Brazil Classics 3: Forró etc.: Music of the Brazilian Northeast
blurb: Compilation of forró and other accordion-led dance music from northeastern Brazil, which David Byrne compared to zydeco. Released on Luaka Bop in 1991.
David Byrne's compilation of samba from Martinho da Vila, Clara Nunes, Beth Carvalho and others. Released on Luaka Bop in 1989.
Third album from Caracas disco-funk band Los Amigos Invisibles, recorded after remixing Beastie Boys and Basement Jaxx. Originally released on Luaka Bop in 2003.
Debut album from Seoul band LEENALCHI, retelling the traditional pansori story Sugungga as psychedelic pop over bass-heavy grooves.
Collaborative project from guitarists Gyan Riley, Devendra Banhart and Noah Georgeson. Gentle instrumental ambient music. Released on Luaka Bop in 2026.

id: I Was Living In a World of Sin (Mixes - Part I)
blurb: Remixes of Annie & the Caldwells' gospel disco by Nicky Siano, Justin Strauss, Kornél Kovács and the musclecars. Released on Luaka Bop.
Five-LP box set of Alhaji Waziri Oshomah's complete Volume Series (1978-1984), the Nigerian Muslim highlife star known as the Oyoyo King. Released on Luaka Bop in 2025.

id: Two Wrongs Don’t Make a Right (Mixes – Part II)
blurb: Second remix EP of Annie & the Caldwells, with Ryan Hope, Rahaan and Alexis Taylor. Released on Luaka Bop in 2025.
Album from Annie & the Caldwells, a family gospel disco-soul band from West Point, Mississippi, led by Annie Caldwell and her husband Willie. Released on Luaka Bop in 2025.
Album from Danish duo Bremer/McCoy, airy instrumental jazz built around bass and keys. Released on Luaka Bop in 2024.
Second album from Mississippi soul-gospel family band the Staples Jr. Singers, made nearly 50 years after their debut after its rediscovery. Released on Luaka Bop in 2024.

id: World Psychedelic Classics 1: Everything is Possible: The Best of Os Mutantes
blurb: Compilation of Os Mutantes, the most outrageous band of late-60s Brazilian tropicália. It introduced them to a generation of listeners outside Brazil. Released on Luaka Bop in 1999.

id: Drill a Hole in That Substrate and Tell Me What You See (Deluxe 20th Anniversary Edition)
blurb: Reissue of Jim White's 2004 album, a cult classic of Southern storytelling featuring Aimee Mann, Joe Henry and Norah Jones, with three extra tracks.
Pharoah Sanders' 1977 album for India Navigation, centred on the 20-minute 'Harvest Time'. Reissued on Luaka Bop as a deluxe box set in 2023.
Contemporary Arabic folk from Iraqi oud player and singer Natik Awayez, with percussion arrangements by Khaled Yassine and oud, violin and buzuq. Released on Sublime Frequencies in 2025.

id: Tsapiky! Modern Music From Southwest Madagascar
blurb: Tsapiky from southwest Madagascar: wild vocals, distorted electric guitars and fast beats, played at funerals, weddings and other ceremonies around Toliara. Released on Sublime Frequencies.
